key_insight: Representing Chain-of-Thought as executable code (Code-as-CoT) gives text-to-image systems precise, structured planning that can be rendered into previews and used to generate rare or complex visual concepts more reliably.
problem_solved: Overcomes the imprecision of natural-language planning in CoT for T2I, which struggles with complex spatial layouts, structured visual elements, and dense textual content.
method: Encode reasoning/planning as executable code (e.g., SVG/HTML/canvas-like scripts or scene descriptions) instead of abstract natural language.
Render the code into a visual preview that conditions a unified multimodal generator, enabling iterative refinement and tighter layout control.
Leverage the explicit code-to-visual mapping to inject and compose rare concepts and structured content more accurately during generation.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to add precise layout control, reproducibility, and better handling of rare/structured concepts to T2I pipelines, improving fidelity for design, OCR-heavy scenes, and compositional tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: text prompt → Code-as-CoT (code block) → preview renderer → image generator (final output)
Before/after examples: natural-language CoT vs Code-as-CoT showing improved layout/text fidelity and rare-concept accuracy
Code snippet + rendered preview pair to illustrate how executable instructions map to visuals
Bar chart or table comparing accuracy/fidelity on spatial, structured-text, and rare-concept benchmarks
paper_title: CoCo: Code as CoT for Text-to-Image Preview and Rare Concept Generation
paper_authors: Haodong Li, Chunmei Qing, Huanyu Zhang, Dongzhi Jiang, Yihang Zou
